summary: Assess climate-water risks, interpret drought indicators, and plan adaptation. Explore the 5-day intermediate course and review the outline.
lede: Training on climate change impacts on water resources helps planners, hydrologists and adaptation professionals assess freshwater risks. They practise screening water-system exposure, interpreting drought indicators and vulnerability evidence, and comparing adaptation options while defining monitoring indicators through spreadsheet-based exercises to inform water allocation and resilience planning.
audienceIntro: This intermediate course is designed for professionals who assess climate-water risks, plan water services, or translate hydrological evidence into adaptation decisions.
prerequisites: Working familiarity with water resources, hydrology, water services, or climate adaptation is recommended. Basic spreadsheet use will support the data exercises; coding or programming is not required. Advanced forecasting and modelling are introduced at conceptual level.
topics: Water & wastewater treatment and utility management
